chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Qaddah, from his father who said:

I lodged at Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Maymoun! Who slumbers with you at night? Is there a slave with you?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do not sleep alone, for the most audacious that the Satan can become, does so upon the human being when he is alone'.
ai.seo_question: Why is it recommended not to sleep alone according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) advises Maymoun al-Azdī to avoid sleeping alone, highlighting the spiritual vulnerability of solitude. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that isolation removes the protective presence of angels and allows Shaytan to act with greater audacity, a concept often linked to the idea of *khawf* (fearfulness) in the chapter title. The advice serves as both a practical safeguard and a spiritual reminder to maintain vigilance (*muraqabah*) even in rest.
